title: LP2-15–22: digit spirals and Roman/HALFMAN selector
question: Do the reported digit-grid contacts and seven-number Roman/HALFMAN result reproduce from archived rune text, and what happens under nearby orientation and window choices?
summary: The 17×17 and 59×59 GP-digit grids, the registered rune-boundary counts, and the selected Roman total of 225 reproduce. Two of 80 local orientation/window cases meet both 225 and descending order, but both reuse the same seven numbers. No rune-to-plaintext rule is supplied.

scope.representation: Archived LP2-15 body runes with nine-rune header excluded, plus all LP2-16–22 runes; each GP prime expanded to ordinary decimal digits. The printed LP2-15 number panel is an independent fixed input for the Roman selector.
scope.procedure: Build center-out right–down–left–up 17² and 59² digit spirals; register the printed 4×4 labels through 1→2, 2→3, 3→N−1, 4→N; check odd-label starts and even-label ends. Transpose the printed panel, take labels 5–11, convert final two digits to Roman numeral first symbols and apply direct HALFMAN ranking. Enumerate eight symmetries and ten consecutive seven-label windows as nearby controls.
scope.parameters: 17×17 and 59×59 streams; sixteen contacts per grid; direct rank order 4,1,5,3,6,2,7; Roman symbols I,V,X,L; target symbol-value sum 225 and descending values. The 80-case scan does not include other word readings, numeric extractions, registrations or permutations.
scope.exclusions: No independent derivation of the five candidate plaintext words; no cipher execution, held-out plaintext, calibrated chance probability or claim that the supplied grids are authorial instructions.

finding: LP2-15 body has 150 runes and 289 GP digits; LP2-16–22 has 1,744 runes and 3,481 GP digits. Under the specified registration, alternating rune-boundary contacts match 12/16 and 16/16. Transposed labels 5–11 give LXLLLXV, rearranged as LLLLXXV by direct HALFMAN ranking; symbol values sum to 225. Exactly 2/80 local orientation-window trials also meet sum 225 and descending order, but both contain the identical seven panel values.
limitations: The representation, source grouping, proposed words, Roman extraction and coordinate map were chosen during exploration. Contacts sharing a rune are dependent. The 80 nearby choices are not the full search space and cannot be read as a p-value. Matching arithmetic does not identify a cipher or decrypt any text.
next_steps: Independently establish the proposed word reading, then freeze one grid registration, route and rune readout before testing an untouched continuation; compare the complete selector with alternative representations and routes.

review.reviewer: Computational replay of pinned manuscript text and supplied PDFs
